incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 288 through 372; particularly Articles 289, 295, 312, 317, 329 and 330
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea, operating through the Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa), together with notarized Articles of Incorporation and the certificate of capital payment
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under the Korean Commercial Act as amended in 2012, a Chusik Hoesa may be incorporated with no statutory minimum paid-in capital and with ordinary shares of KRW 1 par value. There is no administrative blocked-escrow account; however, the aggregate subscription price must be deposited in a Korean bank incorporation deposit account opened by the promoters, and the bank's payment certificate must be submitted at court registration. Foreign-shareholder remittances must be reported to the licensed foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, electronic tax portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr); for outbound customs formalities and export declarations the Korea Customs Service operates UNI-PASS (https://unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Chusik Hoesa organised in Korea files an Application for Business Registration with the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over its principal place of business within 20 days after business commencement. The registration is filed on HomeTax or with an NTS-affiliated tax office manager and produces a 10-digit Business Registration Number used simultaneously for corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding tax. A foreign non-resident entity that has no Korean domestic place of business but is required to register for Korean VAT must appoint a domestic tax representative, file the identical business registration application through the representative, and submit the entity's certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, evidence of authority of the representative, and a statement of the Korean place of supply or business activity. If the entity intends to export cargo from Korea, it additionally registers with Korea Customs Service as an exporter in UNI-PASS to obtain a customs ID for export declarations. The NTS issues the statutory Business Registration Certificate after verification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No flow-through or check-the-box election is available to a Chusik Hoesa; it is a domestic corporation taxed at entity level under the Corporate Tax Act. The only available statutory group election is the consolidated corporate tax base filing mechanism under the Corporate Tax Act if a resident Korean parent owns 100% of the domestic subsidiary, subject to continued ownership and reporting conditions. Korean anti-hybrid rules under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act apply to any hybrid financial instrument or hybrid entity arrangement.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold is provided; every person supplying taxable goods or services in the Republic of Korea is required to register. A simplified taxable person threshold of KRW 80,000,000 in annual turnover applies only to individual entrepreneurs, not to a Chusik Hoesa, and even simplified persons must be registered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered operators must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-Tax Invoice service and transmit invoice data to the NTS by the day following the supply date using the HomeTax web interface, bulk file protocol, or machine-to-machine API. Korea does not impose a pre-clearance fiscal stamping model; instead the NTS clears invoices through real-time database matching of issued and received tax invoice data, VAT returns, customs declarations, and foreign-exchange settlement data. Late, erroneous, or omitted electronic transmission triggers VAT additional tax at prescribed statutory rates.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% VAT applies when a Korean VAT-registered operator exports goods from Korea to a foreign destination and retains customs-accepted export evidence. Project-cargo logistics services performed directly for exported heavy-haul and out-of-gauge cargo are treated as services directly related to exports and are likewise zero-rated, provided the service invoice identifies the relevant export cargo, the purchaser, and the service charge, and the service is paid for by or settled from foreign currency. Where no physical export occurs, zero-rating may still apply to services performed overseas under the place-of-supply rules if the recipient belongs outside Korea and the Korean supplier substantiates the offshore performance and foreign receipt of funds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Export Clearance Certificate) showing the UNI-PASS electronic declaration number and export item description
Original Bill of Lading, Sea Waybill, or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the out-of-gauge cargo from Korea
Commercial invoice and packing list describing out-of-gauge dimensions, weights, marks, and project cargo descriptors
Freight forwarding or project-cargo service contract demonstrating the direct nexus between the zero-rated service and the export shipment
Certificate of Purchase/Sale of Foreign Exchange issued by an authorized foreign exchange bank, or a bank remittance advice showing export proceeds credited in a foreign currency
Out-of-gauge transport permits, route survey, or special haulage approval from the competent road or port authority where required to evidence lawful export movement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: When NTS or Korea Customs Service disallows the zero-rating evidence, the supply is reclassified as taxable and VAT at 10% is assessed on the full supply value, together with additional tax for an unfaithful or fraudulent return under the Framework Act on National Taxes and late-payment interest. A fraudulent claim of export VAT refund is clawed back with punitive surcharges up to 40% of the underpaying amount, and the responsible directors and tax representatives are exposed to criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Offenders Act for deliberate evasion. Customs false declaration penalties and export-restriction sanctions may additionally apply where the export declaration or Bills of Lading are fictitious.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Central Bank of Korea) acting in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates under a managed floating foreign exchange system. The won is freely convertible for current-account transactions, including trade-related payments, dividends, service fees and interest payments, subject to verification through a domestic foreign exchange bank. Capital-account transactions are substantially liberalized, but certain remittances require reporting, registration or approval under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; inbound foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa is recorded through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. No mandatory export surrender ratio is imposed; exporters may retain foreign currency in designated foreign exchange deposit accounts and convert at will. Profit remittance hurdles are primarily documentary: the bank must receive the audited financial statements, corresponding withholding tax payment certificates, minutes of the shareholders' meeting determining the dividend, and evidence of tax clearance before processing the outward dividend remittance. Foreign exchange rates are freely market-determined, and hedging is possible via authorized banks. Speculative foreign exchange transactions by non-financial corporations are restricted, and short-term external borrowing is subject to reporting and monetary policy guidelines. Overall, South Korea offers a highly convertible, institutionally transparent environment suitable for cross-border project cargo heavy haul operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Trade Regulations, export proceeds must be collected within 6 months from the date of the export declaration; an extension of a further 6 months may be granted by the foreign exchange bank with supporting reasons. There is no mandatory conversion requirement and no minimum Korean won surrender ratio; the corporation may hold the entire foreign currency amount in a Foreign Exchange Deposit Account with a licensed Korean bank and later convert at market rates or use it directly for foreign currency payments. Export proceeds received in advance must be settled against the related export declaration within the prescribed periods, and any balance remaining after liquidation can be retained or converted. Failure to collect within the statutory window requires an additional report to the Bank of Korea and may affect the exporter's trade compliance standing.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Under the Korean Banking Act and Electronic Financial Transactions Act, only banking institutions licensed by the Financial Services Commission may lawfully accept KRW deposits and provide corporate payment accounts with local clearing capability. Offshore digital EMI providers without a Korean banking license cannot offer a compliant primary operating account to the Chusik Hoesa; any such solution would be an unlicensed deposit-taking arrangement. EMIs may be used only as an ancillary support for multi-currency card expenses, provided they partner with a Korean bank or hold client funds at a licensed institution, but they are not accepted as core treasury rail for capital verification, export settlements or tax remittance. Consequently the treasury must be structured exclusively through Tier-1 domestic commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa with non-resident individuals as signatories, Korean banks generally require at least one physically present authorized signatory or legal representative at an in-branch interview for account activation. Remote consular proxy opening is permitted under strict conditions, including apostilled power of attorney certified at a Korean consulate, notarized corporate documents, board resolutions, passport copies, and a copy of the business registration certificate; however, many branches still impose an officer visit or video call for enhanced due diligence where the sole director and UBO are foreign natural persons. For a Chusik Hoesa used in heavy-haul project cargo, the relationship manager may additionally request sight of the share registry and corporate bank account opening resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by multi-layer offshore shareholding above the Korean Chusik Hoesa, especially where the ultimate controllers are not individually identifiable from initial corporate registration extracts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an unbroken corporate ownership chain from the Chusik Hoesa to each natural-person UBO, including certificate of incorporation, articles of association, register of directors, register of members, share certificates, notarized passport copies, board resolutions approving share issuance, and a UBO declaration signed under penalty of false statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Extreme mismatch between the registered share capital/funding source and the projected heavy-haul operational cash flows, triggering source-of-funds suspicion for inbound capital escrow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide 6 months of original bank statements from the transferor, audited financial statements of the parent and of the Korean entity, three years of corporate tax returns if available, signed board resolution for capital injection, tax clearance certificate from the sending jurisdiction, and a business plan showing equipment leasing, project cargo route contracts and forecast balance sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-specific trade mispricing or false shipment red flags because out-of-gauge cargo logistics involves high-value contractors and complex multimodal payments that may mirror over or under invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit executed project logistics agreements and purchase orders, sample commercial invoices, customs declarations, bill of lading, freight forwarding contracts for out-of-gauge cargo with dimensional drawings and heavy-lift certificates, insurance policies, subcontractor agreements with crane and barge operators, and a letter from the board designating external counsel to corroborate transaction genuineness.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo concerns if heavy-haul cargos transit, touch, or are destined for jurisdictions or parties subject to international financial restrictions, or if vessel owner and consignee ownership are opaque.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a full counterparty KYC pack, comprehensive sanctions screening results from a commercial provider covering all vessels, beneficial owners and consignees, cargo movement route map with customs pre-clearance confirmations, end-user undertakings, and legal opinion from international trade counsel confirming no nexus to sanctioned parties; additionally appoint a licensed AML officer to oversee affected shipments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The parent or shareholder should remit via SWIFT MT103 to the Chusik Hoesa's Korean escrow or operational account using foreign exchange purpose code 4001 for equity investment or code 3800 for intercompany foreign currency lending under the Korean standard inward remittance classification. For a direct foreign capital contribution, the investor must submit the Foreign Investment Report (No. 4-1) to the Korean foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy via the dedicated system before or immediately after subscription. The bank will register the transaction in the Foreign Exchange Information System and issue a certificate of inward remittance. A statutory CPA performs capital verification by reconciling the bank credit advice, the foreign investment report, the board resolution approving share allotment, the escrow ledger, and the subscribed capital accounts in the Chusik Hoesa's books. For project cargo funding, the capital injection should be segregated in a capital escrow account strictly to evidence clean funding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For global suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 to settle milestone invoices, freight charges, equipment rental and terminal handling fees from the operational currency account; the beneficiary name, purpose code and documentary trail must align with each supply contract. For large purchase of cranes, trailers and specialized rigging gear, an irrevocable sight letter of credit issued by a Korean Tier-1 bank with SWIFT MT700 and confirmed by a foreign advising bank provides the secured payment rail. Documentary collections are accepted for standby or repeat transaction flows where the exporter is familiar and the bill of lading includes out-of-gauge cargo conditions; payments pass through the Korean bank's import settlement department. Domestic KRW disbursements to subcontractors are cleared through the Korea Financial Telecommunications & Clearings Institute (KFTC) funds transfer system via the main bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable Korean won forward contracts executed with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank for actual trade and commercial settlement exposures up to 12 months
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies without Korean onshore usability, subjected to underlying trade documentation and Bank of Korea reporting where required
Cross-currency interest rate swaps limited to hedging external borrowings with a clear economic link to project cargo capex and not for speculative trading
Foreign exchange options purchased for hedging currency risk, with strict prohibition of naked short positions and a mandate to record hedge rationale in each treasury confirm

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세 신고서) with accompanying financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, by March 31 of the following year; extendable to April 30 if the return is prepared by a certified tax agent/CPA.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% non-filing penalty tax on the unpaid corporate income tax; 10% negligent underreporting penalty; 40% fraudulent underreporting penalty; daily late-payment interest at 0.025% per day; coercive seizure and forced collection; criminal referral for willful evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return (법인지방소득세 신고)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local tax authority of the registered office municipality (e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government) via WeTax/자치단체
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate income tax deadline: within 3 months after fiscal year-end; March 31 for a December year-end, or April 30 with a one-month extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty tax of up to 20% for non-filing; 10% for underreporting; daily late-payment interest of 0.025% per day; administrative enforcement proceedings and asset seizure for continued non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Shareholders' Meeting and approval of financial statements, dividend decision, and statutory records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal company records; minutes kept at the registered office. No submission to Companies Registry unless the company is subject to external audit or listing rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; by March 31 for a December fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,750) against responsible officers under the Korean Commercial Act; court order could compel holding; failure to approve financial statements may expose directors to liability and nullify dividend distribution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Management Report (conditional on foreign ownership of 10% or more)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year; by March 31 for a December fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 1,000,000 (approx. USD 750); loss or clawback of foreign investment tax incentives; potential cancellation of foreign-invested enterprise registration status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report filing with the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART (conditional on audit threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) / Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System (DART)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after the annual ordinary general shareholders' meeting; in practice no later than April 30 for a December fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine for negligence of up to KRW 30,000,000 (approx. USD 22,500) for failing to undergo the statutory audit; late or inaccurate FSS filing may result in administrative monetary sanctions and aggravated corporate tax penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Chusik Hoesa is legally required to appoint an independent certified CPA auditor under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if: (a) its shares are listed on the Korea Exchange; (b) its total assets exceeded KRW 12,000,000,000 (approx. USD 9,000,000) at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year; (c) it operates in banking, insurance, securities, or another industry designated by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) regardless of size; or (d) it is designated as an 'other external-audit subject' by the FSC based on revenue, headcount, or public interest. For a private project cargo logistics company, the primary quantitative balance-sheet trigger is the KRW 12 billion total-asset threshold; there is no universal annual turnover or headcount audit trigger for private non-listed logistics companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as adopted by the Korea Accounting Standards Board (KASB) for listed companies and companies subject to external audit; unlisted companies below the audit threshold may apply the Korean Accounting Standards for Small and Medium-Sized Entities (SME-KAS/General Business Accounting Standards) under KASB guidance.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not mandate a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing to the companies registry. Instead, the company must maintain a current Register of Members at its registered office and promptly record all share transfers. Any foreign ownership of 10% or more triggers the Foreign Investment Promotion Act registration with MOTIE via KOTRA and requires subsequent annual management reporting. For AML/CFT compliance, financial institutions must remain satisfied as to the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner at account opening and on an ongoing basis. Any change in directors, registered capital, or other registrable matters must be submitted to the local district court commercial registry within 30 days of the triggering event.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 3,000 per annum for registered office and company secretarial agent services in South Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 20,000 per annum for a certified CPA audit of a small-to-mid-sized project logistics company; higher for consolidated or larger groups

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.0% top marginal national Corporate Tax rate under Article 55(1) of the Korean Corporate Tax Act (tax base above KRW 300 billion), plus a 2.4% local income tax surcharge (10% of national corporate tax) for aggregate top-bracket burden of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive national rates: 9.0% up to KRW 200 million, 19.0% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21.0% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24.0% above KRW 300 billion. Incentives include: 100% corporate tax holiday for 5 years and 50% for 2 years for qualifying foreign-invested high-tech or industrial facility investments under the Special Cases of Taxation Act / Foreign Investment Promotion Act; R&D personnel expenses tax credits (up to 25% super deduction upon NTS approval for qualifying R&D); Investment tax credits under the Integrated Investment Tax Credit; no dedicated patent box in Korea, but IP-derived income from domestically developed technology may be exempt or credited via the Special Cases of Taxation Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (Form 1) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal, with the supplementary 'Statement of International Transactions' and related-party transaction schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final corporate income tax return; semi-annual preliminary corporate tax payments, not quarterly installments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the final corporate tax return must be filed by March 31 of the following year; for other fiscal year-ends, within 3 months after the fiscal year-end. Preliminary corporate tax payments for the first half are due by August 31 and for the second half by November 30 of the taxable year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1: Business registration number, legal identity, representative director, registered address, and industry code (ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal identity, registered office, representative director, business classification code, and a foreign-owner indicator.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean statutory registered office must be a real place of management; an offshore address or mail-drop service will be rejected. The supplementary shareholder schedule must identify every non-resident corporate or individual shareholder and their jurisdiction of tax residence, and changes must be updated before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4: Total sales and ordinary income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross project-cargo, heavy-haul, OOG engineering, port handling, demurrage, and milestone/letter-of-credit revenues accrued under Korean GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate Korean-source service income from foreign-source transport income. Transactions with foreign affiliates must be recorded at arm's-length value; undercharging for completed OOG projects to an offshore parent will trigger transfer pricing adjustment and a 20.0% understatement penalty tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses and cost of sales after statutory disallowance rules, including subcontractor mobilization, cargo equipment, insurance, port charges, and direct overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany service fees, royalties, management fees, and interest paid to non-residents are deductible only if supported by contracts, invoices, evidence of actual benefits conveyed from Korea, and an arm's-length fee. Payments to shell service companies without personnel, assets, or operational functions are disallowed and reclassified as constructive dividends subject to withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit reduced by non-taxable income, tax-exempt reserves, foreign income exemption, and loss carryforward within the statutory 10-year window.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Korean-source profits earned by the Chusik Hoesa from OOG contracts must be included. If NTS determines the Korean entity is a permanent establishment of a foreign principal, no DTA business-profits exemption will shield the Korean-source project income; the PE's attributable profits must be reported in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13: Statutory corporate tax and adjusted total tax after transfer-pricing and withholding adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculated by applying the progressive scale to the tax base, less foreign tax credits, alternative minimum tax, and investment/R&D credits, plus penalty taxes arising from transfer-pricing or withholding corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Statement of International Transactions and the Local File / Master File when the statutory thresholds are exceeded. If the National Tax Service makes an arm's-length income reattribution, the adjusted tax and penalties must be reflected here; a director's certification of prior false deductions makes the director jointly liable for the revised tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file a corporate tax return or filing an understated return triggers penalty tax under Articles 66 and 67 of the Framework Act on National Taxes: 20.0% of unpaid tax for negligent non-filing or under-reporting and 40.0% for fraudulent/aggravated omissions; late-payment interest accrues at the statutory national tax overdue rate from the original due date; the National Tax Service may conduct a forcible collection, seizure, blacklisting (travel ban) and criminal referral for willful tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22.0% aggregate statutory withholding: 20.0% under Article 98 of the Corporate Tax Act plus a 2.0% local income tax surcharge (10% of the 20.0% national tax) on gross dividends paid by a Korean Chusik Hoesa to non-resident corporate shareholders. A bilateral DTA can lower the rate (commonly to 5.0%-15.0%, e.g., 10.0% under many OECD-comparable DTAs for substantial shareholdings).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the Korean payor must obtain, before payment, the non-resident beneficial owner's Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a beneficial-ownership declaration stating no pass-through obligation, and relevant DTA entitlement documentation. The payor then files a treaty-based withholding tax reduction/exemption application on HomeTax for the specific dividend; if the treaty application is approved, the lower DTA rate applies. If the statutory rate has been withheld, the non-resident claimant may file a correction/refund request with the National Tax Service within the statutory assessment period, attaching the TRC and full beneficial ownership evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalty and interest payments by a Korean entity to non-resident corporate recipients are subject to statutory withholding at 22.0% (20.0% national plus 2.0% local surcharge). Treaties commonly reduce interest withholding to 10.0%-15.0% and royalty withholding to 10.0%-15.0%, subject to the recipient's entitlement to limitation-on-benefits, beneficial ownership, and Korean-source characterization; a contracting party failing to substantiate treaty residency will be assessed the full 22.0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in aggregate international related-party transactions triggers contemporaneous Local File and Master File preparation; a multinational group with consolidated revenue of KRW 100 billion or more must also prepare a Country-by-Country Report. Entities below the transaction threshold are still required to disclose international transactions on the annual corporate tax return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations registration system, but the National Tax Service applies a functional Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) analysis and substance-over-form doctrine under Article 3 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and Article 14 of the Framework Act. The Korean Chusik Hoesa managing OOG heavy-haul projects must maintain a Korean board of directors, operate bank accounts and fleet/contract documentation in Korea, employ project engineers and commercial staff locally, and exercise decision-making in Korea; an entity without these functions will be disregarded as a shell and its profits reattributed to the foreign beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Willful failure to withhold and remit non-resident dividend withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors authorize a cash or constructive dividend to a non-resident shareholder at 0.0% withholding, fail to collect Tax Residency Certificate, or classify dividend distributions as intercompany loans/service fees to avoid the Article 98 Corporate Tax Act withholding obligation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the full 22.0% unpaid withholding tax plus a 40.0% fraudulent-omission penalty tax under Article 66 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus daily late-payment interest; the payor is treated as the solely responsible withholding agent and cannot shift the liability to the foreign shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director and board members who approved the distribution are jointly and severally liable for the assessed tax under Article 39 of the Framework Act; unpaid national tax above the serious-arrears threshold triggers travel blacklisting; criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act can result in imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to KRW 100 million.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing mispricing and intentional omission of contemporaneous documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean OOG logistics entity charges foreign affiliates far below arm's-length market rates, makes inflated mobilization or standby payments to an offshore group company, and fails to prepare the Local File/Master File despite the KRW 10 billion threshold being crossed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may re-determine the arm's-length consideration under Article 13 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, adjust taxable income, disallow unsubstantiated deductions, and impose penalty tax of 20.0% for negligent understatement or 40.0% for intentional/manipulated understatement, in addition to late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who certifies false transactional documents or ignores a tax accountant's TP warning may be personally assessed for the resulting corporate tax under joint-liability provisions; continued false documentation can support an aggravated tax-evasion prosecution with imprisonment up to 5 years and personal asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company operation and DTA/treaty abuse (economic substance failure)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Chusik Hoesa has no real Korean office, no locally employed project managers, no board meetings in Korea, and no bank accounts through which OOG project contracts are administered; it merely signs heavy-haul contracts and routes profits through Korea to a foreign parent while claiming treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in Article 14 of the Framework Act and Article 3 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the NTS will disregard the corporate existence for tax purposes, deny DTA benefits, reattribute Korean-source project income to the foreign beneficial owner, impose a 40.0% penalty tax on the understated income, and assess dividend withholding tax on the disguised distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil only where the entity is a fraud or sham; directors become personally liable for corporate tax arrears, plus penalties; they also face civil damages to the tax authority, travel bans for unpaid liabilities, and criminal imprisonment terms up to 5 years or fines up to KRW 100 million under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act.
